feedback.problem:
Find the first two non-zero terms of the Maclaurin expansion of $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+4x+4{x}^{2}).$

$\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+4x+4{x}^{2})=$
{{field-1}}
$+\,\frac{16{x}^{3}}{3}-⋯$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, using the laws of logarithms, we observe that

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+4x+4{x}^{2}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡((1+2x)^{2}) \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+2x).\end{aligned}
$$

The Maclaurin series for $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x)=x-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Replacing $x$ with $2x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+2x) & =(2x)-\frac{1}{2}(2x)^{2}+\frac{1}{3}(2x)^{3}-⋯ \\  & =2x-\frac{1}{2}(4{x}^{2})+\frac{1}{3}(8{x}^{3})-⋯ \\  & =2x-2{x}^{2}+\frac{8{x}^{3}}{3}-⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply the previous expansion by $2$ to obtain the desired result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+4x+4{x}^{2}) & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+2x) \\  & =2(2x-2{x}^{2}+\frac{8{x}^{3}}{3}-⋯) \\  & =4x-4{x}^{2}+\frac{16{x}^{3}}{3}-⋯\end{aligned}
$$
